channel.title: Said & Checked: Maryland — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about Maryland, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Maryland, 2026-11-25: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Jamie Raskin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative: “Reported as: Hadrian Automation, he wrote, received nearly $1 billion in U.S. Navy and Army contracts in March — its first-ever federal contracts — after bringing 1789 Capital on as an investor in 2025.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's federal contract records show one Hadrian award, from the Army in March 2026 ($39.2 million obligated on March 17, about $79.4 million in total by July), and no earlier federal contracts, which fits "first-ever." A Navy contract of about $900 million is reported only in trade press and no award record for it was found, and 1789 Capital's 2025 investment rests on secondary investor lists.
  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative: “Reported as: Juul, Raskin wrote, received Food and Drug Administration clearance to keep its electronic cigarette products on the market in July 2025, four months after 1789 Capital had taken a stake in the company.” Unsettled. FDA's marketing granted orders for Juul's products are dated July 17, 2025, which confirms the July 2025 authorization. The March 2025 date of 1789 Capital's stake appears only in Raskin's own Aug. 26, 2026 letter, which cites Reuters; no primary record of the investment date was found.

item.title: Said & Checked, Maryland, 2026-11-23: 1 contradicted (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “Washington Republicans, they raised and spent twice as much as Democratic Washington Republicans” Contradicted. AskAmerica's FEC data (reports through Oct. 14, 2026) show the Republican national party committees raised about $843 million to the Democratic committees' $725 million and spent $747 million to $710 million; adding the largest allied super PACs on each side gives about $2.1 billion raised to $1.37 billion, roughly 1.5 times, not twice. What remains open: the final pre- and post-election reports are not yet loaded, and the ratio depends on which groups are counted.

item.title: Said & Checked, Maryland, 2026-11-20: 2 contradicted (Steny Hoyer)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Steny Hoyer, U.S. Representative: “In 2013, I helped a group of Democrats and Republicans to reauthorize the Export-Import Bank, over the objections of the chairman of the Financial Services Committee, who was a Republican.” Contradicted. AskAmerica's bill records show Export-Import Bank reauthorizations enacted in 2012 (H.R. 2072, P.L. 112-122) and passed by the House in October 2015 (H.R. 597, 313-118, after a discharge motion), while 2013 Ex-Im bills were only referred to committee; the 2015 bill's text amends the 2012 act, with no 2013 act between them. Hoyer's own role and the chairman's opposition were not assessed, and the warehouse holds no 2013 House roll calls, so a 2013 vote under another title is not fully ruled out.
  • Steny Hoyer, U.S. Representative: “The decade between fiscal year 2001 and fiscal year 2010, we averaged 108 days a year under continuing resolutions.” Contradicted. CRS R42647's Table 3 gives total days under continuing resolutions for fiscal 2001-2010 of 82, 102, 143, 123, 69, 92, 365, 92, 162 and 79, an average of about 131 days a year, not 108; leaving out fiscal 2007's full-year resolution gives about 105. What remains open is whether the figure comes from a different counting method.

item.title: Said & Checked, Maryland, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Jamie Raskin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative from Maryland: “It spread across the Colonies and became the best-selling book of all time, other than the Bible, in the Colonies.” Unsettled. Sources describe Common Sense as a sensation (the Thomas Paine Society cites over 500,000 copies) but note that historians dispute the copy counts, and none ranks it against the Bible.
  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative from Maryland: “George Washington had the troops at Valley Forge read the words of ``Common Sense'' to each other by campfire light” Unsettled. No record was found of Common Sense being read to troops at Valley Forge. The commonly told story is that Paine's The American Crisis was read before the Delaware crossing in December 1776, and a Journal of the American Revolution article says even that story lacks documentary evidence. No primary Washington papers were read.
  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative from Maryland: “That recommendation has yet to be transmitted to Congress, which has slowed down our work.” Unsettled. The AP reported in January 2026 that the National Capital Memorial Advisory Commission recommended Area I placement in September 2024 and that the Interior Secretary must endorse it before it goes to Congress. No record was found showing whether it has since been transmitted.

item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “We have two senators-elect who would not be there if the current majority leader had his way” Unsettled. Reporting conflicts on whether Sen. Schumer publicly endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan (one outlet says he endorsed her; another says leadership had only a private preference). In Minnesota no public backing of Peggy Flanagan's opponent by Schumer, the DSCC or Senate Majority PAC was found, only reports of a private preference. Figures are as reported by news outlets; no official record covers private preferences.

item.title: Said & Checked, Maryland, 2026-11-15: 1 false, 1 contradicted (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “And I chair the subcommittee that oversees the Department of Commerce that helped expose his involvement with the -- with Epstein.” False. The Senate Appropriations Committee's own page for its Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittee lists Jerry Moran as chair and Chris Van Hollen as ranking member, and AskAmerica's committee roster shows the same. Republicans hold the Senate majority until the new Congress is seated in January. The second part of the sentence, on what the subcommittee helped expose, was not checked: no page read addressed it.
  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “Republicans in Washington raised twice as many funds.” Contradicted. AskAmerica's Federal Election Commission data for the 2026 cycle show the three Republican national party committees with receipts of $843.1 million (RNC $341.5 million, NRCC $263.8 million, NRSC $237.8 million) against $725.5 million for the three Democratic committees (DNC $252.3 million, DCCC $256.8 million, DSCC $216.4 million): about 16 percent more, not twice. The FEC's own 18-month summary gives the same ratio. Still open: super PACs and other outside groups, which were not counted.
